serialFormats.description: Carrier / Bryant / Payne modern style: WWYY + plant letter + 5-digit sequence (e.g. 3018E12345 = week 30 of 2018)
sources: Carrier 48TC*D08-D14 Service and Maintenance Instructions, Appendix I — Model Number Nomenclature / Serial Number Format (manualsdir.com/manuals/59708/carrier-48tcd08.html?page=87)
Building Intelligence Center — Carrier HVAC age (building-center.org/carrier-hvac-age/)
Building Intelligence Center — Bryant HVAC age (building-center.org/bryant-hvac-age/)
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
Inspector Handbook — Decode Carrier HVAC Serial Number (inspectorhandbook.com/hvac/carrier)
notes: Positions 1-2 = week of manufacture (01-53), positions 3-4 = year, position 5 = manufacturing plant letter, positions 6-10 = sequence. Carrier's own 48TC service-manual appendix documents this layout; building-center.org dates it from ~1980 (Carrier) / 1985 (Bryant) and it is still in use.
Pivot 70: '85'-'99' -> 1985-1999, '00'-'69' -> 2000s. Weeks above 53 mean you are not reading a Carrier serial (e.g. ICP YYWW style puts the year first).

Only the two sourced examples (3216E54321 from hvacbase.org, 3018E12345 from the task brief / hvacagelookup format description) carry a third-party-stated date; the 1993 and 2005 examples are constructed to exercise the pivot and are consistent with the documented rule.
Plant letter map is not published in the sources gathered; common letters seen on light-commercial rooftops are E, G, V and C. Not decoded here.
Canadian-built units are reported (building-center.org) to swap the year/week positions; if week > 53 on a Canadian nameplate, try YYWW.

ICP brands (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite) use the same 10-character look but with YEAR first (see icp-yyww). A leading letter + 4 digits is ICP; 4 digits + letter is Carrier/Bryant/Payne.

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1960s-1970s: 1-2 digit week, then a year letter (L=1960 ... H=1979, skipping O, Q, Z), then 5 digits (e.g. 12E12345 = week 12 of 1976)
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Carrier HVAC age (building-center.org/carrier-hvac-age/)
Grokipedia — Carrier serial number decoding (grokipedia.com/page/Carrier_serial_number_decoding)
notes: building-center.org: year letter (2nd or 3rd position) begins with L and cycles to H, skipping O, Q and Z, representing 1960-1979; week is the leading 1-2 digits. Grokipedia gives the worked example 12E12345 -> week 12 of 1976, which agrees with the map (E = 1976).
The 1974 example is constructed from the rule, not from a dated nameplate. Letters L-W map to 1960-1969, below the engine's 1965 floor; treat any such decode as 'pre-1965, confirm on plate'.
No collision with the modern WWYY style (that one has four digits before the letter) or with the 1970s letter-month style (that one starts with a letter).

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1970s: month letter A-L (Jan-Dec), then one year digit (197x), then 5 digits (e.g. E312345 = May 1973)
sources: Grokipedia — Carrier serial number decoding (grokipedia.com/page/Carrier_serial_number_decoding)
PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
notes: PickHVAC and Grokipedia agree: one letter A-L = month, first digit = year within the 1970s, then a sequence. Grokipedia's worked example E312345 -> May 1973 is the sourced test; K712345 is constructed from the rule.

Collides with the Bryant 1980s letter-month + two-digit-year style (B85xxxx = Feb 1985): E852345 reads 1978 here and 1985 there. Disambiguate by nameplate brand/style, R-22 vs earlier refrigerants, and the 1980s-style rectangular Bryant plates; the engine will flag the ambiguity.

serialFormats.description: Carrier 1980-1988 'Style 3': month letter M-Z, one year digit (198x), a letter, then 5 digits (e.g. S5D16399 = June 1985). Year only is decoded; month letters are not fully mapped.
sources: PickHVAC — Carrier HVAC Age: Serial Number Breakdown (pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/carrier/)
notes: Single secondary source (PickHVAC): 8-character serial, letters M-Z for the month, second character = year digit within the 1980s (0 = 1980 ... 8 = 1988). Its worked examples: S5D16399 = June 1985, Z1D27364 = December 1981, R8D16382 = May 1988.

The month-letter map implied by those examples (R = May, S = June, Z = December) is not self-consistent with a simple M=January sequence, so the month is deliberately not decoded. Read the year only and confirm the month from the compressor date code.
Low confidence: memory and one decoder site only. Carrier product support or the distributor can date these from the serial directly.

serialFormats.description: Bryant/Payne 1980s all-numeric 9-character style: YYMM + 5-digit sequence (e.g. 830812345 = August 1983)
sources: Building Intelligence Center — Bryant HVAC age (building-center.org/bryant-hvac-age/)
Grokipedia — Carrier serial number decoding (grokipedia.com/page/Carrier_serial_number_decoding)
notes: building-center.org (Bryant): nine numeric characters used primarily in the 1980s; positions 1-2 = year, 3-4 = month. Grokipedia's transitional example '83081...' = August 1983 agrees. Both examples here are constructed to that rule (the sourced example is truncated in the source), hence low confidence.
Era-clamped to 1980-1989. A 9-digit serial with positions 3-4 > 12 is not this style (ICP YYWW without plant letter is 10 characters).

serialFormats.description: Bryant/Payne 1980s: month letter A-L then two-digit year then sequence (e.g. B85xxxxx = February 1985)
sources: bryantnorthwest.com — How to Tell the Age of Your Bryant Furnace
HVAC Base — Carrier HVAC Age: How to Tell AC Age by Serial Number (hvacbase.org/carrier-hvac-age-serial-number)
notes: bryantnorthwest.com and hvacbase.org describe older Bryant serials as a month letter (A = January ...) followed by the two-digit year (B85 = February 1985). Sequence length is not documented; the regex accepts 4-6 trailing digits.

Collides with Carrier's 1970s letter-month + one-digit-year style when the year digits are 8x (see carrier-monthletter-yeardigit-1970s). Confirm with the brand on the plate and the compressor date code.

serialFormats.description: ICP brands (Tempstar, Heil, Comfortmaker, Arcoaire, Day & Night, KeepRite, Airquest): optional plant letter + YYWW + sequence (e.g. L943321238 = week 33 of 1994)
sources: icptempstarparts.com — Serial Number Nomenclature (ICP / Tempstar / Heil)
Intry — ICP Serial Number Lookup (intrysys.com/tools/hvac/serial-number-lookup/icp)
InspectApedia — Tempstar HVAC Age, Manuals (inspectapedia.com/heat/Tempstar-HVAC-Age-Manuals.php)
notes: icptempstarparts.com, Intry and InspectApedia agree: plant letter (sometimes omitted) + 2-digit YEAR + 2-digit WEEK + sequence; ICP puts the year before the week, the opposite of Carrier/Bryant/Payne. Sourced example: L943321238 = week 33 of 1994. The 2001 and 2015 examples are constructed from the rule.

Because the year comes first, an ICP serial reads with year and week swapped relative to Carrier's WWYY style (ICP '1523...' = week 23 of 2015; a Carrier '1523G...' would be week 15 of 2023). The plant-letter position separates them (ICP letter first, Carrier letter fifth); an all-digit 10-character serial is ambiguous unless week > 53 rules one out. Confirm with the brand on the nameplate: Tempstar/Heil/Comfortmaker/Arcoaire/Day & Night/KeepRite -> ICP rule.
ICP nameplates carry ICP nomenclature (RGH/RAH/RGS/RAS/RHS ... for light-commercial rooftops) even though the serial style is shared with Carrier since UTC/Carrier ownership.

controls.name: Carrier Integrated Gas Controller (IGC) — LED flash codes
controls.description: Gas-heat ignition/safety board on 48-series rooftops (48TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC/JC, 48A/P/N gas sections, legacy 48HJ/TJ/TM/TF/EJ, Bryant 580J/581J, ICP RGH/RGS). One status LED: steady ON = normal, OFF = no power or hardware failure, N flashes = fault. Codes are displayed until the fault clears or power is cycled.

faultCodes.meaning: Hardware failure (no power to IGC, or the board has failed).
likelyCauses: No 24 VAC at IGC (TRAN, fuse/CB, door switch)
Failed IGC board
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the IGC power terminals; if present with LED off, replace IGC
Check the 24 V control fuse / circuit breaker and transformer secondary

faultCodes.meaning: Indoor fan on/off delay modified — the IGC has shortened the fan on/off delay after a limit-switch trip or heating fault.
likelyCauses: Prior limit-switch trip (low airflow: dirty filters, slipping belt, closed dampers, wrong fan speed)
Excessive supply-air temperature rise
checks: Check filters, belt and blower; measure temperature rise against nameplate range
Clear by cycling power after fixing airflow

faultCodes.meaning: Limit switch fault — high-temperature limit switch is open.
likelyCauses: Low airflow (dirty filter, loose belt, blower/motor fault, wrong drive/speed)
Supply-air temperature rise above nameplate range
Failed limit switch
checks: Check indoor (evaporator) fan motor operation and belt
Measure supply-air temperature rise; it must be within the range on the unit nameplate

faultCodes.meaning: Flame sense fault — the IGC sensed flame that should not be present.
likelyCauses: Gas valve leaking through / stuck open

Inspect flame sensor lead for grounds; measure flame current

faultCodes.meaning: Four consecutive limit switch faults — lockout.

Reset by cycling 24 V power to the IGC (or thermostat call) after correcting airflow

faultCodes.meaning: Ignition lockout — unit failed to prove flame (typically after 4 ignition attempts / 15 tries on some versions).
likelyCauses: No gas / low gas pressure
Igniter not sparking or spark gap wrong
Flame sensor dirty or misplaced
Gas valve not opening (no 24 V, failed valve)
Poor burner/flame carryover
checks: Verify inlet and manifold gas pressure during trial

faultCodes.meaning: Induced-draft motor fault — IDM/pressure switch did not prove or lost proving during a cycle.

faultCodes.meaning: Rollout switch lockout — the rollout switch has opened.
likelyCauses: Flame rollout from blocked heat exchanger or flue
Delayed ignition (low gas pressure, dirty burners, cross-over problems)

likelyCauses: Failed IGC board

faultCodes.meaning: Temporary software lockout — the IGC has locked out for 1 hour after repeated faults; resets automatically or on power cycle.
likelyCauses: Repeated ignition/limit faults within a short period
checks: Address the underlying fault (see the prior code); cycle power to clear
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48TC / 48HJ / 48TF / 48EJ Installation and Service Instructions — 'IGC Board LED Alarms' / 'LED Error Code Service Analysis' table (e.g. 48HJD005-007 IOM p.39; 48TFD008-014 IOM p.42; 48EJ IOM p.60); tsihvac.com igc_codes.pdf (same table)
faultCodes.notes: From memory of the IGC table; verify against the IOM.

ledPatterns.meaning: No 24 V power to IGC or board hardware failure
checks: 24 VAC at IGC input
control fuse / CB

ledPatterns.pattern: LED flashing N times, pause, repeat

diagnosticTips: The IGC LED is on the board in the gas-section control compartment (burner side); view it with the panel open and the door-interlock (if fitted) bypassed for service only.

Codes 2, 3, 7 and 8 were confirmed against Carrier IOM pages this session; codes 1, 4, 5, 6 and 9 are from memory of the same table — verify in the unit's IOM 'IGC Board LED Alarms' before acting on them.
To clear a lockout: remove the call for heat (W) for a few seconds or cycle 24 V control power; rollout switches (7 flashes) are manual reset at the switch.
The IGC controls the indoor fan in heating: fan starts ~45 s after the burners light and runs ~45 s after W drops out; a modified delay shows as 1 flash.
Heat-exchanger limit trips on rooftops are almost always airflow: check filters, belt tension, blower rotation and the supply-air temperature rise against the nameplate range before condemning parts.

Fire alarm system relay contact
Shorted/mis-wired input
checks: Check smoke detector status LEDs and reset
Verify the input's configured normal state

faultCodes.meaning: Shorted or open circuit on the SAT input.
likelyCauses: SAT thermistor open/shorted
Wiring or plug fault
checks: Ohm the 10 k thermistor at the board (about 10 kΩ at 77 °F); check the SAT wiring to the supply duct/discharge

faultCodes.meaning: In a linked (zoned) system the RTU Open lost communication with its linkage master, or received data from more than one master zone.
likelyCauses: Network wiring / addressing
Duplicate linkage master configuration
checks: Check the network bus and the master zone controller address
Ensure only one linkage master

faultCodes.code: Space Temp Sensor / Dirty Filter / Fan Status / Compressor Status alarms
faultCodes.meaning: Additional configurable alarms documented in the RTU Open integration guide: space temperature sensor failure, dirty filter (differential switch), supply fan status (no proof), compressor status/failure, OAT sensor, IAQ/CO2 sensor, space temp high/low, SAT high/low.
likelyCauses: Sensor or switch fault, or a real condition (filter loaded, belt broken, compressor safety open)
checks: Read the alarm text and the associated status point on the Equipment Touch / BAS; the point name identifies the input to test
faultCodes.source: Carrier RTU Open v3 Integration Guide (11-808-521-01) / RTU Open v5 Integration Guide (11-808-697-01) — Alarms section; RTU Open Controls, Start-Up, Operation and Troubleshooting (manualslib 1955294) — Alarms (list names from memory; verify in the guide)

diagnosticTips: Connect with Field Assistant (USB Local Access) or the Equipment Touch to view alarms, points and to run the controller's Service Test (fan, compressors, heat, economizer).

Set the protocol and baud with the DIP switches and rotary address switches on the board; the board's status LEDs (Run/Error) indicate firmware state — Error LED patterns are in the installation guide.
Alarms reset automatically when the condition clears unless configured as latching; check 'Alarm settings' for the enable flags before assuming a missing alarm means no fault.

controls.name: Carrier ComfortLink rooftop / applied controls (48/50A, P, N, Z, PG/PM Centurion, 48/50HC v3, 38AP/30RAP scrolling marquee)
controls.description: Carrier's proprietary DDC with scrolling-marquee display (later Navigator / touch display). Alerts are 'Txxx' (unit keeps running with reduced function) and alarms 'Axxx' (component or unit shutdown). Code numbers follow a family-wide scheme: 05x compressors, 11x loss of charge, 12x/13x pressure switches and safeties, 14x-17x sensor failures, 2xx fan/economizer/configuration, 3xx service/compressor stuck. Replaces the previous 10 from-memory entries. Every code above was seen in a search-result snippet from a Carrier manual page (ManualsLib/ManualsDir page titles or excerpts) or, for T500-T507, in an aggregated snippet of the table (marked single_secondary). Numbering is shared across the ComfortLink rooftop family but a few 4xx codes differ between the 48/50HC v3 table and the 48/50PG C03-14 table: HC T410 = 'Fan Status Switch OFF, fan commanded on' and T411 = 'R-W1 jumper not installed', whereas PG C03-14 uses T409 = fan status off/contactor on, T410 = R-W1 jumper, T411 = Thermostat Y2 without Y1. Always read the expanded text on the display. T051/T055 text differs by family: 48/50HC (one compressor per circuit) shows 'Compressor A1/B1 Safety Trip'; 48/50A/P/N multi-compressor units show 'Circuit A/B, Compressor n Failure' (T051-T057). High-head threshold: 150°F saturated condensing on 48/50HC, 145°F on 48/50AJ/AK/AW/AY. Not found in any source and therefore omitted: A153, A290 (requested by the task), and the remaining 1xx/2xx/3xx/4xx codes of the full table (e.g. T140/T14

faultCodes.meaning: 48/50HC: Compressor A1 Safety Trip — indicates high-pressure switch open, internal protection open, or wiring error. 48/50A/P/N (multi-compressor circuits): Circuit A, Compressor 1 Failure — compressor feedback signal (current sensor board) does not match relay state.
likelyCauses: HPS open on circuit A (manual text)
Compressor internal overload / internal protection open (manual text)
Incorrect safety or compressor wiring, tripped circuit breaker (manual text)
Failed contactor or current sensor board (CSB) so no current is seen for 4 s after the relay is commanded on (manual text)
checks: Turn the compressor on in Service Test; if it does not start the manual says the likely problem is HPS open, circuit breaker trip, incorrect safety wiring or incorrect compressor wiring
Check 24 V through the compressor safety string to the contactor coil and confirm contactor pull-in (field practice)
Measure compressor amps and compare with the CSB feedback in the STATUS/INPUTS menu (field practice)
Each occurrence adds a strike to the compressor; 3 strikes lock the circuit out (A163) — clear the cause before resetting
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T051 Compressor A1 Safety Trip' and 'To check out alerts T051, T052, T055, T056' paragraph; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 'Circuit A, Compressor 1 Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A, Compressor 2 Failure — if the current sensor board reads OFF while the compressor relay has been commanded ON for 4 continuous seconds an alert is generated; a strike is called out on the affected compressor.
likelyCauses: HPS open, circuit breaker trip, incorrect safety wiring or incorrect compressor wiring (manual text)
Failed contactor or CSB (field practice)
checks: Run compressor A2 in Service Test; if it does not start check HPS, breaker, safety and compressor wiring (manual text)
Verify CSB feedback and compressor amps (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 'Compressor Alarm/Alert Circuit' — T052

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A, Compressor 3 Failure — compressor feedback (CSB) does not match relay state for 4 s.
likelyCauses: As T051/T052 for compressor A3
checks: As T051 for compressor A3 (Service Test, safety string, CSB feedback)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 — T053

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A, Compressor 4 Failure — compressor feedback (CSB) does not match relay state for 4 s.
likelyCauses: As T051/T052 for compressor A4
checks: As T051 for compressor A4
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 — T054

faultCodes.meaning: 48/50HC: Compressor B1 Safety Trip — indicates high-pressure switch open, internal protection open, or wiring error. 48/50A/P/N: Circuit B, Compressor 1 Failure — compressor feedback signal does not match relay state.
likelyCauses: HPS open on circuit B, internal protection open, wiring error (manual text)
Breaker trip, failed contactor or CSB (manual/field)
checks: Run compressor B1 in Service Test; if it does not start check HPS, breaker, safety wiring, compressor wiring (manual text)
Verify contactor pull-in, compressor amps and CSB feedback (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T055 Compressor B1 Safety Trip'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'Circuit B, Compressor 1 Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B, Compressor 2 Failure — compressor feedback (CSB) does not match relay state for 4 s.
likelyCauses: As T051/T052 for compressor B2
checks: As T051 for compressor B2
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 — T056

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B, Compressor 3 Failure — compressor feedback (CSB) does not match relay state for 4 s.
likelyCauses: As T051/T052 for compressor B3
checks: As T051 for compressor B3
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 / ComfortLink 6 Series p.42 — T057

faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor Air Temperature Thermistor Failure — no cooling with economizer. Cause: faulty, shorted, or open thermistor caused by wiring error or loose connection. Clears automatically.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted OAT thermistor or wiring, loose plug (manual text)
checks: Compare the OAT reading in the TEMPERATURES menu with a reference thermometer; ohm the thermistor at the MBB plug against the thermistor table in the controls manual (field practice)
Economizer free cooling and OAT-based lockouts are disabled while active
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T073 – Outdoor Air Temperature Thermistor Failure'; 48/50HC-05T Table 9 T073

faultCodes.meaning: Space Temperature Thermistor Failure — if U.CTL = 3 (space sensor control) then no heating or cooling. Cause: faulty, shorted, or open thermistor caused by wiring error or loose connection. Clears automatically.
likelyCauses: T-55/T-56 space sensor or its wiring open/shorted; loose connection (manual text)
Unit configured for space sensor (U.CTL = 3) with no sensor installed (field practice)
checks: Check U.CTL configuration matches the installed control (thermostat vs space sensor)
Ohm the space sensor at the field terminals; check sensor wiring for shorts to ground (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T074 – Space Temperature Thermistor Failure'; 48/50HC-05T Table 9 T074

faultCodes.meaning: Supply Air Temperature Thermistor Failure — no cooling with economizer and no adaptive compressor staging. Cause: faulty, shorted, or open thermistor caused by wiring error or loose connection. Clears automatically.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted SAT thermistor or wiring; loose plug (manual text)
checks: Ohm the SAT at the MBB plug against the thermistor table; verify the reading in the TEMPERATURES menu (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T075 – Supply Air Temperature Thermistor Failure'; 48/50HC-05T Table 9 T075

faultCodes.meaning: Return Air Thermistor Failure — if RAT.S = Yes then no differential dry bulb control. Cause: faulty, shorted, or open thermistor caused by wiring error or loose connection. Clears automatically.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted RAT thermistor or wiring (manual text)
checks: Ohm the RAT at the board plug; check RAT.S configuration if no RAT sensor is fitted (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T076 – Return Air Thermistor Failure'; 48/50HC-05T Table 9 T076

faultCodes.meaning: Space Relative Humidity Sensor Failure — if RH.S = Yes then no indoor humidity control. Cause: faulty, shorted, or open sensor caused by wiring error or loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty space RH sensor, 4-20 mA loop wiring open/shorted (manual/field)
checks: Check the RH sensor supply and 4-20 mA signal at the board; verify RH.S configuration (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T077 – Space Relative Humidity Sensor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Return Air Relative Humidity Sensor Fail.
likelyCauses: Faulty return-air RH sensor or its wiring (field practice)
checks: Check sensor power and signal at the board input; verify configuration for the installed sensor (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier WeatherExpert 48N2 controls manual p.118 alert table 'T078 Return Air Relative Humidity Sensor Fail'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12

faultCodes.meaning: Mixed Air Relative Humidity Sensor Fail.
likelyCauses: Faulty mixed-air RH sensor or its wiring (field practice)
checks: Check sensor power and signal at the board input; verify configuration (field practice)
faultCodes.source: Carrier WeatherExpert 48N2 controls manual p.118 'T079 Mixed Air Relative Humidity Sensor Fail'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit C Saturated Condensing Temp Thermistor Failure (units with a third circuit).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted circuit C condensing thermistor or wiring (field practice)
checks: Ohm the circuit C SCT thermistor at the board plug (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.39 'Alert Code T080 – Circuit C Saturated Condensing Temp Thermistor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Space Temperature Offset Sensor Failure — occurs if the potentiometer is outside the allowable range.
likelyCauses: Faulty offset slider potentiometer on the T-56 space sensor or its wiring (manual/field)
checks: Ohm the offset potentiometer wires at the sensor and at the board; check for a shorted/open slider (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Code T082 – Space Temperature Offset Sensor Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure — occurs when the unit is configured for pressure and the board does not properly read the transducer voltage (pressure outside 0.0-667.0 psig). A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty discharge pressure transducer (manual text)
Faulty 5 V transducer supply from the board (manual text)
Loose or corroded transducer connector (manual text)
checks: Compare the PRESSURES menu reading with a gauge on circuit A discharge
Check 5 Vdc supply and signal at the transducer plug; swap with the circuit B transducer to isolate (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T090/T091 – Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure — pressure outside the range of 0.0 to 667.0 psig. A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: As T090 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T090/T091 – Discharge Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Suction Pressure Transducer Failure — occurs when the board does not properly read the transducer voltage (pressure outside 0.0 to 420.0 psig). A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty suction transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: Compare PRESSURES menu suction reading with a gauge; check 5 Vdc and signal at the plug (field practice)
A failed suction transducer can also produce A140 reverse-rotation or T110 loss-of-charge nuisance alarms — fix it first
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T092/T093 – Suction Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Suction Pressure Transducer Failure — pressure outside the range of 0.0 to 420.0 psig. A circuit cannot run when this alert is active. Cause is usually a faulty transducer, faulty 5-v power supply, or a loose connection.
likelyCauses: Faulty transducer, faulty 5 V supply, loose connection (manual text)
checks: As T092 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T092/T093 – Suction Pressure Transducer Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Loss of Charge — indicates low refrigerant or faulty suction pressure transducer.
likelyCauses: Refrigerant leak / low charge (manual text)
Faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
checks: Compare standing suction pressure on circuit A with saturation pressure at ambient; leak-check if low (field practice)
Verify the suction transducer reading against a gauge (T092 may accompany a bad transducer)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T110 Circuit A Loss of Charge'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T110 Circuit A Loss of Charge'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Loss of Charge — indicates low refrigerant or faulty suction pressure transducer.
likelyCauses: Refrigerant leak / low charge; faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
checks: As T110 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T111 Circuit B Loss of Charge'; 48/50AJ Table 114 T111

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A High Discharge Pressure (48/50A: Circuit A High Head Pressure) — active while the circuit's saturated condensing temperature is greater than 150°F (48/50HC; 145°F on 48/50AJ/AK/AW/AY) and resets automatically. Cause is usually an overcharged system, high outdoor ambient temperature coupled with dirty outdoor coil, plugged filter drier, or a faulty high-pressure switch.
likelyCauses: Overcharged system (manual text)
High outdoor ambient plus dirty outdoor coil (manual text)
Plugged filter drier (manual text)
Faulty high-pressure switch (manual text)
Failed/slow outdoor fan motor (field practice)
checks: Check condenser coil cleanliness and OFM operation; measure head pressure and subcooling (field practice)
Check liquid-line temperature drop across the filter drier
Verify the HPS opens/closes at rated pressure
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T126/T127 – Circuit High Discharge Pressure'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T126 Circuit A High Head Pressure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B High Discharge Pressure (48/50A: Circuit B High Head Pressure) — saturated condensing temperature greater than 150°F (145°F on 48/50AJ); resets automatically.
likelyCauses: Overcharge, high ambient with dirty coil, plugged filter drier, faulty HPS (manual text)
checks: As T126 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T126/T127'; 48/50AJ Table 114 'T127 Circuit B High Head Pressure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Low Refrigerant Pressure — low suction pressure while the compressor is operating. Auto resets, but is only allowed to reset a limited number of times before the circuit is locked out and A163 is generated.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant pressure / low charge (manual text)
Faulty suction pressure transducer (manual text)
Restricted airflow: dirty filters, broken belt, iced evaporator (field practice)
Restricted metering device or filter drier (field practice)
checks: Check suction pressure with a gauge against the PRESSURES menu; check superheat and charge (field practice)
Check indoor airflow, filters and coil; check for ice on the evaporator
Check history for repeated T133 leading to A163 lockout
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T133/T134 – Circuit Low Refrigerant Pressure'; 48/50AJ Table 114 ('low refrigerant pressure alarms T133, T134 handle the situation when the compressor is operating')

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Low Refrigerant Pressure — low suction pressure while the compressor is operating; repeated trips lock out the circuit (A164).
likelyCauses: Low charge, faulty suction transducer, airflow restriction (manual/field)
checks: As T133 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T 'Alert Codes T133/T134'; 48/50AJ Table 114

faultCodes.meaning: Reverse Rotation Detected — a test is made once, on power up, for suction pressure change on the first activated circuit: the suction pressure of both circuits is sampled 5 seconds before the compressor is brought on and right when the compressor starts; if the expected drop is not seen the control declares reversed phasing and the unit is not allowed to start.
likelyCauses: Incoming three-phase power leads phased incorrectly (scroll compressor running backward) (manual text)
Dirty or failed suction pressure transducer, or broken transducer wire, giving no pressure change (HVAC-Talk field reports)
Compressor did not actually start (contactor, breaker) during the test (field practice)
checks: Check outdoor/indoor fan rotation first; if reversed, swap two incoming power leads at the disconnect (manual text)
If rotation is correct, verify the suction transducers read correctly against gauges and clean/replace the transducer or repair its wiring (HVAC-Talk field reports)
Manual reset: clear the alarm and cycle power to re-run the power-up test
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T / 48/50A-14T 'A140 (Reverse Rotation Detected)' paragraph; Carrier 38APS p.171 'A140 — Reverse Rotation Detected'; HVAC-Talk 'Carrier Alarm Codes A140' thread

faultCodes.meaning: Unit is in Emergency Stop — the CCN emergency stop command has been received; the unit shuts down. Listed as T150 (alert) on some tables and A150 (alarm) on others.
likelyCauses: CCN/BAS EMSTOP command active (manual text)
checks: Check the CCN/building-automation system for an active emergency-stop point and release it; alarm clears automatically once EMSTOP returns to normal (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 'T150 / A150 Unit is in Emergency Stop'; 30RAP ComfortLink table 'A150 Emergency Stop — CCN emergency stop command received'

faultCodes.meaning: Unit Down Due to Failure — unit shut down due to alarms/alerts (all circuits are down due to alarms/alerts and the unit is unable to run). Also generated when LEN (Local Equipment Network) communication is lost.
likelyCauses: Both circuits locked out by other alarms (A163 + A164) (manual text)
Loss of LEN communication between MBB and the other boards (manual text)
checks: Read ALARMS > CURR for the underlying alarms and clear those first; A152 resets automatically once the alarms that prevent starting are cleared (manual text)
Check LEN bus wiring/plugs (J3/J4) and that the green LEN LED is blinking on every board (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A152 Unit shut down due to alarms/alerts'; 48/50AJ Table 114 / 30RAP table 'A152 Unit Down Due to Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Real Time Clock Hardware Failure — the real-time clock on the Main Base Board has failed.
likelyCauses: MBB real-time clock hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Re-set the time/date in the CLOCK menu and cycle power; if the alert returns replace the MBB (field practice)
Occupancy schedules are unreliable while active
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code T153 – Real Time Clock Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Serial EEPROM Hardware Failure — hardware failure of the configuration EEPROM on the Main Base Board.
likelyCauses: MBB EEPROM hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if the alarm persists the MBB must be replaced (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code A154 – Serial EEPROM Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Serial EEPROM Storage Failure Error — a non-critical configuration value could not be stored/read from the EEPROM.
likelyCauses: EEPROM write error on the MBB (manual text)
checks: Verify configuration values and re-enter any that have reverted; cycle power; replace MBB if repeating (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code T155 – Serial EEPROM Storage Failure Error'

faultCodes.meaning: Critical Serial EEPROM Storage Fail Error — a critical configuration value could not be stored/read from the EEPROM; the unit will not run.
likelyCauses: EEPROM failure on the MBB (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if it returns replace the MBB and reconfigure (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50PG C03-14 p.40 'Alarm Code A156 – Critical Serial EEPROM Storage Fail Error'

faultCodes.meaning: A/D Hardware Failure — the analog-to-digital converter on the Main Base Board has failed.
likelyCauses: MBB A/D hardware fault (manual text)
checks: Cycle power; if the alarm persists replace the MBB (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50AJ Table 114 / 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12 'A157 A/D Hardware Failure'

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit A Down Due to Failure — lockout of circuit A; manual reset. Probable cause: circuit has 3 strikes or has been locked out by another alarm. (Service Test text: 'Circuit A Down Due to Failure'.)
likelyCauses: Three strikes from T051-series compressor safety trips or T133 low-pressure trips (manual text)
Circuit locked out by another alarm (manual text)
checks: Read ALARMS > HIST to find the alerts that produced the strikes; correct that fault
Reset by clearing current alarms (ALARMS menu) after repair; the circuit stays locked out until manually reset (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A163 Circuit A Down Due to Failure' (Lockout Circuit A, Manual reset)

faultCodes.meaning: Circuit B Down Due to Failure — lockout of circuit B; manual reset. Probable cause: circuit has 3 strikes or has been locked out by another alarm.
likelyCauses: Three strikes (T055-series or T134) or lockout by another alarm (manual text)
checks: As A163 for circuit B
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A164 Circuit B Down Due to Failure' (Lockout Circuit B, Manual reset)

faultCodes.meaning: Linkage Timeout Error – Comm Failure — the Main Base Board has lost communication with a previously connected Linkage device (the MBB is no longer receiving commands from a Linkage network such as an EMS or building automation system).
likelyCauses: Linkage master (VVT/3V zone controller, i-Vu, EMS) offline or removed (manual text)
CCN bus wiring fault or duplicate/changed address (field practice)
checks: Check the CCN bus wiring and the linkage master; verify the yellow CCN LED blinks on the MBB during communication (manual/field)
If the linkage device was intentionally removed, cycle power to clear the stored linkage (manual text)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A200 Linkage Timeout – Comm Failure'; 48/50PG C03-14 Table 12

faultCodes.meaning: Fire Shutdown — unit shutdown occurs when smoke is detected by the smoke detector (fire shutdown input active).
likelyCauses: Smoke detector (supply or return) tripped (manual text)
Fire-shutdown/fire-alarm system contact open, or the FSD input wiring/jumper missing (field practice)
Dirty smoke detector head giving a nuisance trip (field practice)
checks: Find and clear the smoke source first; reset the smoke detector
Check the fire-shutdown input contact and wiring at the field terminal board; confirm the fire-alarm panel is not holding the contact (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'A404 Fire Shutdown — Unit Shutdown, smoke detected'

faultCodes.meaning: Dirty Air Filter — indicates a plugged filter (filter status switch input); alert generated automatically.
likelyCauses: Plugged filters (manual text)
Filter status switch set too sensitive or misconfigured input (field practice)
checks: Replace filters; verify the filter status switch setpoint and that the input is configured for filter status (field practice)
faultCodes.source: 48/50HC-05T Table 9 'T408 Dirty Air Filter'; 48/50PG C03-14 p.43 'Alert Code T408 – Dirty Air Filter'

faultCodes.meaning: Fan Status Switch ON, fan commanded off (Fan Status Switch On/Fan Contactor Off) — indicates a bad fan status switch or configuration incorrect.

Broken belt (manual text)

Incorrect input configuration or bad fan status switch (manual text)

diagnosticTips: Scrolling marquee: 4-digit display with ESCAPE / ENTER / up / down keys on the main control box. Hold ESCAPE to reach the top menu; the ALARMS menu shows CURR (current) and HIST (history) codes; RCRN = reset current alarms.

Service Test mode: from the SERVICE TEST menu set TEST = ON (unit must be off / disabled) to run fans, compressors, heat stages, economizer and power exhaust manually — the manual lists lockouts that remain enforced.
Alerts (Txxx) do not shut the unit down; alarms (Axxx) do. Codes with the same number can appear as T or A depending on whether the fault is inhibiting a component or the whole unit.

ALL codes above are from memory of the 48/50A / 48/50HC ComfortLink alarm tables and are marked inferred — read the unit's controls manual 'Alarm and Alert Codes' appendix (48/50A-15T for 48/50A; 48/50HC-05T for 48/50HC v3; 48/50PG C03-14 for Centurion) before acting. 38AP and 30RAP use different chiller/condensing-unit tables.

Display: the ComfortLink Scrolling Marquee is a 4-key, 4-character, 16-segment LED module on the main control box (ESCAPE, ENTER, up, down). Menus: Run Status, Service Test, Temperatures, Pressures, Setpoints, Inputs, Outputs, Configuration, Time Clock, Operating Modes, Alarms. The accessory Navigator (handheld) or i-Vu/CCN can also be used.

Reading an alarm in plain English: press ESCAPE to clear the marquee, scroll to ALARMS, press ENTER on CURR (currently active alarms) or HIST (alarm history); when a code is displayed press ESCAPE and ENTER at the same time to expand it — the display scrolls the full alarm text plus time/date (48LC controls manual p.3; HVAC-Talk).

Resetting alarms: ALARMS menu contains CURR (current alarms), HIST (alarm history) and R.HIS / reset items; the manual says to use the Scrolling Marquee to reset the alarm after correcting the cause. Lockout alarms (A163/A164) are manual reset; most T-alerts clear automatically when the condition goes away.

Service Test: set SERVICE TEST > TEST = ON from the marquee (the marquee writes a Control force at level 7; the Navigator writes a Service force at level 3). Service Test lets you run the indoor fan, compressors, heat stages, economizer and power exhaust individually; several alerts have a 'Service Test' variant text. In space-sensor mode the R-W1 jumper must be installed to run heat in Service Test (T411).

Alerts (Txxx) let the unit keep running with reduced function; alarms (Axxx) shut down a circuit or the unit. Compressor safety trips and low-pressure trips accumulate strikes; 3 strikes lock the circuit out (A163/A164) until manually reset.

Board LEDs: MBB has a red STATUS LED, a green LEN LED (should always blink) and a yellow CCN LED (blinks with traffic). Gas units: the IGC LED flash code is read on the IGC board in the heat section (see ledPatterns). Some ComfortLink RTUs ask for a service access code on the display: factory default is commonly 1111 (HVAC-Talk field reports — confirm in the unit's manual).

ledPatterns.pattern: IGC (integrated gas control) LED ON steady
checks: No action

ledPatterns.meaning: Hardware failure — no power to the IGC or failed board.
checks: Check 24 V to the IGC and its fuse; replace IGC if powered and dark (field practice)
Informational: the fan delay jumper/setting has been changed from default

ledPatterns.meaning: Limit switch fault — high-temperature limit switch is open.
checks: Check indoor airflow (filters, belt, blower), limit switch continuity, and heat exchanger temperature rise (field practice)

ledPatterns.meaning: Flame sense fault — the IGC sensed flame that should not be present.
checks: Check for a leaking/stuck gas valve, flame sensor shorted to ground, or wiring; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: 4 consecutive limit switch faults — inadequate airflow to the unit.
checks: Correct airflow (filters, belt, motor, dampers) then reset power (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Ignition lockout fault — the unit unsuccessfully attempted ignition for 15 minutes.
checks: Check gas supply and pressure, igniter, flame sensor, gas valve; reset at the unit disconnect (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Induced-draft motor fault — the IGC does not sense that the induced-draft motor is operating.
checks: Check IDM operation and the speed/hall-effect feedback wiring to the IGC (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Rollout switch fault — the rollout switch has opened. The rollout switch will automatically reset, but the IGC will continue to lock out the unit; reset at the unit disconnect.
checks: Find the cause of flame rollout (blocked heat exchanger/flue, low airflow, burner problems) before resetting (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Internal control fault — the microprocessor has sensed an error in the software or hardware.
checks: Cycle power; replace the IGC if it repeats (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Main Base Board processor running; the red LED on each board should blink in sync with the others, with the MBB as the lead board.
checks: If blinking is absent or asynchronous suspect a board communication issue: disconnect the LEN/CCN plugs and check resistance on the communication lines; check LEN connections at J3/J4 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Local Equipment Network active — should always be blinking whenever power is on.
checks: If not blinking check board power and LEN wiring; a lost LEN can generate A152 (manual text)

ledPatterns.meaning: Carrier Comfort Network communication in progress — blinks only while CCN traffic is present.
checks: Steady off with a BAS connected: check CCN bus wiring, address and baud rate (field practice)

controls.name: EconoMi$er IV / EconoMi$er2 (Honeywell W7212 analog economizer controller)
controls.description: Analog economizer controller used on 48/50TC/HC and legacy 48/50HJ/TJ (2003-~2014). No fault codes: diagnosis is by the three LEDs (Free Cool, DCV, Exhaust) and terminal voltages. EconoMi$er2 is the same damper package driven by a DDC controller (PremierLink / ComfortLink / RTU Open) via 4-20 mA instead of the W7212.

faultCodes.meaning: The W7212 has no displayed fault codes. Free Cool LED on = outdoor air suitable (economizing enabled); DCV LED on = demand-control-ventilation active (CO2 above setpoint); Exhaust LED on = power exhaust output energized.
likelyCauses: Damper not moving: no 24 VAC at TR/TR1, actuator failure, enthalpy sensor (C7400) failed
Free Cool LED never lights: enthalpy setpoint too low, outdoor enthalpy sensor open, jumper/DIP configuration
Damper stuck open in occupied: minimum-position pot set high, or 2-10 VDC signal fault
checks: Measure 24 VAC between TR and TR1
Measure 2-10 VDC at the actuator (P/P1 minimum position pot); 2 V = closed, 10 V = open
Simulate a low outdoor enthalpy: jumper SO/+ per the IOM checkout table and confirm Free Cool LED and damper open
Check the C7400 enthalpy sensor at SO/+ (should read ~3-25 mA depending on enthalpy)
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC Installation Instructions — 'EconoMi$er IV' / 'EconoMi$er2' sections and W7212 troubleshooting table
faultCodes.notes: From memory of the 48TC IOM economizer checkout; verify in the unit's installation instructions.

ledPatterns.meaning: Outdoor conditions suitable — economizer allowed to modulate for cooling
CO2 above setpoint — damper driven toward the DCV maximum position
Power exhaust relay energized (damper past the exhaust setpoint)

diagnosticTips: The W7212 is mounted on the economizer damper assembly or in the control box; potentiometers set minimum position, DCV max, exhaust setpoint and the enthalpy changeover (A/B/C/D or 1-6 on later units).
With the W7212 removed from a unit with a DDC controller (PremierLink/RTU Open/SystemVu), the damper is driven directly by the controller (EconoMi$er2) — do not look for the W7212.
Frozen evaporator or high humidity with the unit off often traces to a damper that fails to close (spring-return actuator failure or minimum position set too high).

controls.description: Base-unit-controls option 0 on 48/50TC/HC/FC/GC/KC and all legacy 48/50HJ/TJ/TM/TF and 38AU/40RU splits: relays, contactors, CLO/compressor lockout board, IGC for gas heat, driven by a 24 V thermostat (R, C, G, Y1, Y2, W1, W2). Faults are found by tracing 24 V through the safety strings; the only 'codes' are the IGC LED (gas units) and the CLO / phase-monitor LEDs.

faultCodes.meaning: The compressor lockout (CLO) relay/board has opened the compressor circuit after a safety (HPS, LPS, freeze stat) opened during a call; it latches until the thermostat call is removed (Y) or control power is cycled.
likelyCauses: HPS trip (condenser airflow, overcharge)
LPS trip (low charge, low airflow / iced coil, low ambient)
Freeze protection thermostat open
checks: Check 24 V across each safety in the string (HPS, LPS, FPT) with the call active; the open one drops the 24 V
Reset by removing the Y call at the thermostat (or cycling the disconnect); if it retrips, diagnose the pressure condition with gauges
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC Installation Instructions — 'Compressor Lockout' / troubleshooting section (from memory; verify)

faultCodes.meaning: Phase monitor relay (PMR) has dropped out for phase loss, reversal or imbalance; its LED indicates fault vs normal per the label on the relay.
likelyCauses: Rotation reversed at the unit disconnect
Lost phase / blown fuse
Voltage imbalance > 2-3 %
checks: Measure all three line voltages; swap two incoming leads if rotation is reversed (scroll compressors must rotate correctly)
Read the PMR label for LED meaning
faultCodes.source: Carrier 48/50TC IOM — phase monitor option (from memory; verify)

diagnosticTips: Sequence check: jumper R to G (fan), R to Y1 (compressor 1 + OFM), R to Y2 (compressor 2), R to W1 (IGC heat) at the low-voltage terminal board to isolate the thermostat from the unit.
The low-voltage terminal board (TB) is in the main control box; the 24 V transformer (TRAN) usually has a 208 and 230 primary tap — set it to the measured line voltage.

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling, electromechanical: thermostat closes R-G (IFC energizes IFM) and R-Y1; 24 V passes through the circuit-1 safety string (HPS, LPS, FPT, CLO contact) to C1, starting compressor 1 and the OFM. On two-stage units R-Y2 energizes C2 (compressor 2) the same way. Opening of any safety drops C and, on CLO-equipped units, latches the compressor off until Y is removed.

Cooling with economizer: with outdoor air suitable (Free Cool LED / W7220 'economizing'), Y1 first modulates the outdoor-air damper between minimum position and full open to hold the mixed-air setpoint (~50-55 °F); mechanical cooling is added (Y1/Y2 passed to compressors) only when free cooling cannot satisfy or when outdoor air is not suitable. On DDC units (RTU Open/SystemVu) the controller stages compressors and drives the damper itself.

Heating (gas): thermostat closes R-W1. The IGC verifies the limit and rollout switches are closed, starts the IDM, proves the draft pressure switch, energizes the spark igniter and opens the gas valve; flame must be sensed within the trial period or the IGC retries and eventually locks out (LED 5 flashes). The IGC energizes the IFM ~45 s after ignition. W2 opens the second stage of the two-stage gas valve on medium/high-heat units. When W drops out the gas valve closes, IDM post-purges and the IFM runs ~45 s more.
Heating (electric heat on 50-series): W1/W2 energize the heater contactors through the heater's own limit switches; the IFM runs with G or through the heater relay.
Heat pump (50TCQ/HCQ): O/B reversing valve energized in cooling on Carrier (verify on diagram); defrost is time/temperature initiated by the defrost board.
notes: Designators and sequence are the standard Carrier light-commercial rooftop legend from memory of the 48/50TC IOM; the IOM was not read this session, so treat as low-confidence and confirm on the unit's own wiring diagram (inside the control-box door).

Phase monitor: available as a factory option on 48/50TC 3-phase units and standard on 48/50TC 17-30 and newer SystemVu-equipped units (F206 alarm); scroll compressors run backwards (noisy, no pumping) if rotation is reversed — check on start-up.
Single-phase (voltage code 3 / Bryant J) sizes 04-07 use a PSC/ECM IFM and capacitor-start compressor; there is no PMR.

Newer (2023+) builds add a Low Pressure Switch bypass timer and, on R-454B (48/50JC) units, refrigerant detection sensors (RDS) that force the IFM on and lock out ignition/compressors on a leak alarm.

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat cycles on limit / IGC shows 2 or 4 flashes; supply air very hot
likelyCauses: Low airflow: loaded filters, slipping or broken belt, blower wheel dirty, IFM on wrong speed tap or wrong drive setting
Supply dampers/VAV boxes closed
Over-fired: manifold pressure high or wrong orifices for altitude/gas
checks: Measure temperature rise (supply − return) and compare to the nameplate range
Check belt tension/condition and blower rotation; measure external static
Check manifold pressure (typ. 3.5 in. w.c. natural gas high fire; see nameplate)

commonIssues.symptom: No heat, IGC LED 5 flashes (ignition lockout) — especially first cold snap of the season
likelyCauses: Flame sensor coated (low microamps)
Igniter cracked / spark gap wrong
Gas pressure low (regulator, closed valve) or gas valve not energized
Spiders/debris in burners causing poor carryover
checks: Watch the trial: spark present? gas valve 24 V? flame lit then dropped (sensor) or never lit (gas/igniter)?
Clean the flame sensor with fine abrasive pad and re-check flame current
Verify inlet pressure under load and manifold pressure

commonIssues.symptom: Heat works, but indoor fan will not shut off or will not start in heating (cooling fan OK)
likelyCauses: IGC board fan relay contacts welded or failed (common IGC failure)
IGC 1-flash modified delay after limit trips
checks: With no calls, check for 24 V on the IGC fan output; if present with W off, replace IGC
Check limit history (2/4 flashes) and airflow before replacing the board

commonIssues.symptom: Compressor won't run; 24 V present at Y but contactor coil dead (CLO tripped)
likelyCauses: HPS trip: dirty condenser coil, OFM/capacitor failed, overcharge
LPS trip: low charge, iced evaporator, low ambient without low-ambient control
FPT open on evaporator coil
checks: Remove the Y call to reset CLO, then watch pressures at restart
Check OFM runs and condenser coil is clean; check subcooling/superheat
Check FPT continuity with the coil warm

commonIssues.symptom: 3-phase scroll compressor loud, low amps, no pressure differential after install or after a power outage/utility work
likelyCauses: Reverse rotation (phase sequence changed)
Lost phase (single-phasing)
checks: Check phase sequence at the unit; swap two incoming leads at the disconnect only
Verify all three line voltages under load and imbalance < 2 %
On units with PMR/F206, read the phase monitor LED

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer damper stuck open or never opens; high humidity / high indoor temp; iced evaporator in winter
likelyCauses: W7212 EconoMi$er IV: failed C7400 enthalpy sensor, failed actuator, minimum-position pot mis-set
W7220 EconoMi$er X: missing/failed S-bus OAT sensor (no free cooling), actuator alarms, MAT sensor error
Broken damper linkage / seized damper blades
checks: Command the damper open/closed (W7220 CHECKOUT menu, or 2-10 VDC test on W7212) and watch travel
Check 24 VAC at the actuator and the 2-10 VDC / S-bus signals
Inspect linkage and blade seals; verify minimum position with the fan running

commonIssues.symptom: Water in the unit / condensate overflow or drain pan not draining
likelyCauses: No trap or wrong trap depth on the drain (draw-through evaporator is under negative pressure)
Drain line plugged with slime
Unit not level / pan cracked
checks: Verify a properly sized trap per the IOM (deeper than the fan's negative static in in. w.c.)
Clear and flush the drain; check the pan drains with the blower running

commonIssues.symptom: Belt-drive blower: squeal on start, low airflow, high supply temperature rise; frequent belt replacement
likelyCauses: Belt tension / worn or misaligned pulleys
Motor pulley set for wrong RPM (variable-pitch pulley)
Bearing failure on blower shaft
checks: Check belt deflection and pulley alignment; check pulley groove wear with a gauge
Measure IFM amps vs FLA and external static; adjust pulley per the fan performance table

commonIssues.symptom: Humidi-MiZer unit: poor dehumidification, or cooling weak with the reheat coil hot
likelyCauses: 3-way valve / solenoid stuck in reheat position
Humidistat or DDC dehumidify input wiring
Reheat check valve leaking
checks: Verify the dehumidify input state and 24 V at the valve solenoids
Compare liquid-line and reheat-coil temperatures in normal cooling — reheat coil should be near liquid temperature when not in reheat

commonIssues.symptom: SystemVu/RTU Open unit runs but BAS shows sensor alarms; readings drift from measured values
likelyCauses: Thermistor wiring shared with line-voltage conduit (induced noise)
SAT sensor mounted too close to the heat exchanger / in radiant view
Loose plug on the MBB
checks: Compare the controller reading to a calibrated probe at the sensor location; reseat plugs
Relocate SAT downstream per the IOM if it reads high with heat on

commonIssues.symptom: Legacy R-22 rooftop (48HJ/TJ/TM/TF): repeat compressor failures / slugging
likelyCauses: Refrigerant migration on long off cycles (no crankcase heater on many small sizes)
Overcharged after retrofit to an R-22 replacement blend
TXV flooding from a loose/insulated-badly bulb
checks: Check superheat at the compressor after 10 min run; confirm bulb mounting
Weigh in the charge per nameplate when a retrofit refrigerant is used; confirm the refrigerant on the retrofit sticker

commonIssues.symptom: Unit dead, no 24 V: transformer secondary fuse/CB open
likelyCauses: Shorted thermostat wire (rubbed on cabinet)
Shorted contactor coil or economizer actuator
TRAN wired to wrong primary tap (208 vs 230) overheating
checks: Isolate: disconnect the field thermostat wires at TB; if the fuse holds, the short is in the field wiring
Ohm contactor coils and check the economizer 24 V load
Verify the transformer tap matches measured line voltage

Nameplate reading: Carrier commercial rooftop plates list MODEL NO., SERIAL NO., electrical data (volts/phase/Hz, MCA, MOP, compressor RLA/LRA, fan FLA), refrigerant and charge per circuit, and test pressures. Decode only the MODEL NO. line; ETO / 'Product No.' strings are not the model.

Light-commercial model layout (48/50TC, HC, LC, FC, GC, KC): 10 characters, dash, 5 option characters. Positions: 1-2 unit type, 3-4 series, 5 heat size, 6 electrical options, 7-8 size code, 9 intake/exhaust, 10 base-unit controls, 11 design revision, 12 voltage, then packaging/refrigerant-system/service/fan/coil options.

Refrigerants: 48/50TC/HC/LC/FC/GC/KC, 38AU, 40RU, 38AP, 30RAP/30RB, 48/50A2-A5, P, N = R-410A (Puron); legacy HJ/TJ/TM/TF/EJ, AJ-AY, Z, 30RA, 09DK = R-22 (verify retrofit sticker); 48/50JC (2025+) = R-454B (A2L) — confirm on plate.
